title: Jeffreys prior as a named invariance recipe
dek: π(θ) ∝ √det I(θ). Wikipedia 'uninformative' celebrity that is quite informative on some scales. stats-priors owns elicitation.
story: Jeffreys' prior on Wikipedia is π(θ) ∝ √det I(θ), famous for invariance under reparameterisation. It is a recipe, not a certificate of ignorance.
On a Bernoulli π it is Beta(1/2,1/2), which piles mass near 0 and 1 — sometimes exactly where a TB rare-event probability lives. Calling it uninformative is a slogan.
stats-priors is the elicitation plate. This card is the named recipe so a paper that says 'we used a noninformative prior (Jeffreys)' can be interrogated.
deep: Improper Jeffreys priors can make marginal likelihoods/Bayes factors undefined.
Independence Jeffreys versus full Jeffreys in multiparameter models is a fork.
Reference priors are a neighbouring more elaborate recipe.
A lab-informed Beta on a DST error rate can beat Jeffreys on calibration.

visual.caption: Schematic Beta(1/2,1/2)-like pile-up at the edges versus a flatter Beta(1,1). Jeffreys is not 'no information' on the probability scale.
